headline: High-risk shared-write and API-driven pair: Devin can alter shared workspaces and external systems while Superset can consume shared data, creating dangerous default pathways for leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can write files, use MCP, and act autonomously in shared integrations; Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. A plausible bridge exists if Devin places attacker-controlled content into shared workspace or API-fed artifacts that Superset later interprets. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Devin writes untrusted text into a shared workspace or integration payload that Superset later parses as instructions
IF Superset ingests content from Devin without provenance or sanitization
mitigations: Restrict Devin to a non-shared workspace folder
Disable any Superset ingestion of free-form agent-generated text
Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent artifacts
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like content
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between agent outputs and Superset inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, and can write to cloud workspace files and integrations. Superset is open-source with allowlisted egress and a Superset API, so if it receives Devin-produced artifacts containing sensitive data, leakage can occur through dashboards, exports, or API-backed workflows. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF Devin places source code, chat, or secret-bearing artifacts into a workspace readable by Superset
IF Superset exports or serves those artifacts through dashboards or API responses
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared dataset before handoff
Limit Superset datasets to redacted copies
Audit one dashboard for sensitive columns
Rotate any exposed integration token immediately
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and analytics workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, shell, and broad network egress in a shared cloud workspace; Superset has allowlisted network egress and a Superset API. If both operate on the same mutable resource, Devin can overwrite or race with Superset-managed state, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive. Uncertainty about Superset write scope does not reduce the risk because the shared mutable surface is plausible and unguarded.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository, dataset, or config directory
IF no external lock or transaction guard is enabled
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Pause one agent during commits or dataset updates
Use branch-per-agent workflow
Check for concurrent writes before merge
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can generate artifacts and act inside integrations; Superset can consume API-backed data and present it downstream. If Superset treats Devin-produced outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into dashboards or operational decisions. The profiles do not prove blind trust, so medium is appropriate, but the interaction is still default-plausible.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Devin-generated metrics, SQL, or annotations without validation
IF downstream users act on Superset-rendered outputs as ground truth
mitigations: Require a human review step before publishing dashboards
Compare one sample metric against source data
Mark Devin-generated fields as untrusted
Restrict Superset to read-only consumption of vetted tables
requires-engineering: add validation rules for agent-produced inputs

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles source code, team chat, docs, and secrets via cloud workspace integrations, while Superset is an analytics platform with no stated residency or retention controls in the profile. If regulated data is moved from Devin into Superset, retention or residency mismatches could create a compliance gap. Only Devin is cited because Superset lacks compliance metadata; that absence itself increases uncertainty and pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF regulated data from Devin is loaded into Superset
IF Superset retention or residency differs from the source system
mitigations: Classify data before loading it into Superset
Exclude secrets and regulated fields from analytics
Document retention for one dataset
Verify hosting region for the Superset deployment
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
